questions.q: How does Prepare Mass Additions derive the depreciation expense account for a new line?
options: It always uses a fixed default account for all categories
It asks the user to manually enter the account for every line
It copies the account from the previous month's depreciation run
It overlays the invoice distribution's clearing account with the natural account segment of the depreciation expense account defined on the asset category
questions.explain: Prepare Mass Additions takes the clearing account combination and overlays its natural account segment with the natural account segment of the category's depreciation expense account.

questions.q: What queue status indicates a Mass Additions line where required information (like the expense account) could not be derived?
options: New
On Hold
Post
Posted
questions.explain: On Hold is the status Prepare Mass Additions assigns when it cannot derive required information for a line.

questions.q: What was the actual root cause of all six delivery truck lines being stuck On Hold?
options: Six unrelated data entry errors
The trucks were not yet delivered
The new asset category 'Vehicles - Delivery Trucks' had no depreciation expense account defined for the book, so no line using that category could derive one
The accounting period was closed
questions.explain: A single category-level setup gap (missing expense account) affected every line using that category, which is why all six were held for the same reason.

questions.q: Why was it correct to re-run Prepare Mass Additions for all six lines together rather than processing them individually?
options: Because the root cause was a single category-level fix; once applied, the derivation would succeed for every line using that category in one pass
Because Oracle requires batch processing for all Mass Additions
Because individual processing is not technically possible
Because the trucks had sequential invoice numbers
questions.explain: Since the fix was at the category level (adding the missing expense account), a single re-run of Prepare Mass Additions resolved all six lines at once.

questions.q: What process improvement does the resolution note recommend to prevent this from recurring?
options: Disable the ability to create new asset categories
Require all new assets to use an existing category only
Manually enter the expense account on every future invoice line
A checklist step confirming full category setup (cost, accumulated depreciation, and expense accounts) whenever a new category is created
questions.explain: The note recommends verifying that all required accounts are defined on a new category before it is used, to avoid this kind of batch hold recurring.
